items.title: The Eighth Numeric Category Opens: The Eightfold Path as Three Trainings, Eight Kinds of Noble Person, and Seven Flawed Ways to Give Against One Flawless Way

items.zh: 已說七種佛教所應知處。次說八種。謂有八支聖道所攝，令諸苾芻究竟斷結三種修法。謂修戒、修定、修慧。正語、正業、正命，名為修戒；正念、正定，名為修定；正見、正思惟、正精進，名為修慧。又由正方便及果增上力故，建立清淨品八種補特伽羅。謂行四向、住四果者。又有二種施，八相差別。一、有過失施，二、無過失施。前七種施，名有過失；最後一種，名無過失。謂有布施懈怠所損，故有過失。或有布施不隨所欲，故有過失。謂有染心者，怖畏貧窮、悕求富樂而行布施。或有布施顧戀過去，故有過失。或有布施悕望未來，故有過失。或有布施有輕慢過，故有過失。或有布施悕求富樂，故有過失。或有布施求他知聞，故有過失。無過失施者，謂迴向涅槃故，為彼資糧故，無染污心為往善趣故，為得大財故，而行布施。
items.en: The seven-thing category of what a Buddhist should know has now been explained. Next, the eight-thing category. There are three trainings, comprised within the eight-limbed noble path, that let monks ultimately sever the fetters: the training of precepts, the training of concentration, and the training of wisdom. Right speech, right action, and right livelihood are called the training of precepts; right mindfulness and right concentration are called the training of concentration; right view, right intention, and right diligence are called the training of wisdom. By the power of correct method and its fruit, eight kinds of pure person are established: those practising towards each of the four fruits, and those abiding in each of the four fruits. There are also two kinds of giving, with eight distinguishing marks: flawed giving, and flawless giving. The first seven kinds are flawed; the last alone is flawless. There is giving harmed by laziness, and so flawed. There is giving that does not follow what one truly wishes, and so flawed — namely, one with a defiled mind gives out of fear of poverty or desire for wealth and pleasure. There is giving that dwells on the past with regret, and so flawed. There is giving that hopes for future return, and so flawed. There is giving tainted by contempt, and so flawed. There is giving that seeks wealth and pleasure, and so flawed. There is giving that seeks to be known and heard of by others, and so flawed. Flawless giving is giving dedicated to nirvāṇa, giving as a provision towards it, giving with an undefiled mind for the sake of a favourable rebirth, and giving in order to obtain great wealth [for others' benefit].

items.title: Eight Moments a Lazy Mind Always Finds an Excuse, and the Same Eight Moments a Diligent Mind Finds a Reason

items.zh: 又依四處，於八時中，趣入懈怠，不發精進。當知如是補特伽羅是懈怠類，非精進類。謂依乞食處，依所作處，依遊行處，依界不平等處。依此四處，八時差別。多食精美，身沈重時；少食麁惡，身劣頓時；將欲所作，護惜力時，已有所作，身疲倦時；將欲遊行，護惜力時；已涉長塗，身疲倦時；正為病苦所纏擾時；所病已愈，恐更發時。此懈怠類補特伽羅，乃至未遇懈怠所依，少似精進；若得遇已，速發懈怠；是故名為懈怠種類。與此相違，亦依四處，於八時中發勤精進。當知如是補特伽羅能伏懈怠，勤精進類。
items.en: Depending on four circumstances, in eight moments, one turns towards laziness and fails to arouse diligence: know that such a person belongs to the class of the lazy, not the diligent. Namely, depending on almsround, on undertaking a task, on travel, and on bodily imbalance. Depending on these four, there are eight distinct moments: when the body feels heavy from eating too much rich food; when the body feels weak and sluggish from eating too little or too coarsely; when about to undertake a task, sparing one's strength; when a task is finished, the body fatigued; when about to travel, sparing one's strength; when a long journey is finished, the body fatigued; when actually afflicted by illness; and when illness has just passed, fearing its return. Such a lazy person, until meeting one of these occasions for laziness, appears somewhat diligent; but once the occasion arises, laziness swiftly follows — hence called the class of the lazy. The reverse of this — also depending on the same four circumstances, in the same eight moments, arousing diligence — know that such a person, capable of subduing laziness, belongs to the class of the diligent.

items.zh: 雖遇懈怠所依，亦能發勤精進，何況不遇，是故名為勤精進類。
items.en: Even when they meet with occasions for laziness, they can still arouse diligent effort, let alone when they do not; that is why they are called the class of the diligent.

items.title: Eight Desirable Places to Be Reborn, for Those Not Yet Seeking to Leave the Desire Realm Entirely

items.zh: 又有八種正願所攝可愛生因，能令於諸欲中樂增上生，不求永離一切欲者，當生八種可愛生處。謂願人中卑惡種類，修小施戒二福業事；如是願樂人中尊貴種類、四大王天、三十三天、夜摩天、覩史多天、樂化天、他化自在天、修小施戒二福業事。
items.en: There are also eight causes of a desirable rebirth comprised within a correct aspiration, capable of leading one who delights in the desire realm and does not yet seek to leave all desire entirely to a favourable rebirth there, to be born in eight desirable places: wishing for birth among the lowly castes of humanity, one cultivates giving and precepts in modest measure; and likewise wishing for birth among the noble castes of humanity, or in the Heaven of the Four Great Kings, the Heaven of the Thirty-Three, the Yāma Heaven, the Tuṣita Heaven, the Heaven of Delighting in Transformation, or the Heaven of Mastery over Others' Transformations, one cultivates giving and precepts in modest measure.

items.title: Eight Assemblies Among Humans and Gods, and the Eight Worldly Winds No Being Escapes

items.zh: 又四因緣故，於人趣中建立如來四眾；三因緣故，於天趣中建立四眾。最增上故，世間共許為福田故，受用資財不由他故；棄捨一切世資財故；由此四緣，於人趣中建立四眾。依地邊際故，欲界邊際故，語行邊際故；由此三緣，於天趣中建立四眾。又於世間三處轉時，恒常世間八法所觸。謂樂欲處、功用處、眾緣處。於樂欲處轉時，或觸於利，或觸非利。於功用處轉時，或稱他意，或不稱意；於背面位觸於毀、譽，於現前位觸於稱、譏。於眾緣處轉時，或由先世、或由現法苦樂眾緣，觸於苦、樂。
items.en: By four causal conditions, the Tathāgata's four assemblies are established among humans; by three causal conditions, four assemblies are established among gods. Being of the highest standing; being universally acknowledged as a field of merit; enjoying one's own resources without depending on others; and having renounced all worldly resources entirely — by these four conditions, four assemblies are established among humans. By the boundary of the earth; by the boundary of the desire realm; and by the boundary of verbal activity — by these three conditions, four assemblies are established among gods. Further, in three situations that recur throughout the world, one is constantly touched by the eight worldly phenomena: the situation of desire and aspiration, the situation of effortful action, and the situation of manifold conditions. In the situation of desire, one is touched either by gain or by its absence. In the situation of effortful action, one either meets others' approval or does not; behind one's back, one is touched by censure or praise; face to face, one is touched by acclaim or blame. In the situation of manifold conditions, whether from past lives or from present causes and conditions of pain and pleasure, one is touched by pain or by pleasure.

items.title: The Eight Liberations Revisited as Eight Resolves, Specifically Drawing Out Superknowledge and the Cessation Attainment

items.zh: 又八勝解，能引不還、或阿羅漢諸聖神通及最勝住。謂未伏內色想，外無染污色勝解，是名第一；已伏內色想，是名第二；淨不淨非二色第一捨勝解，是名第三。此三解脫，於一切色得自在故，便能引發諸聖神通。謂諸神通不與一切異生共有。空無邊勝解、識無邊勝解、無所有勝解、非想非非想勝解、微微任運心勝解，此五勝解次第善修治故，能引想受滅等至最勝住。
items.en: There are also eight resolves, capable of drawing out the noble superknowledges of a non-returner or arhat, and the supreme abiding. The resolve of not yet having subdued the perception of inner form, together with the resolve of undefiled outer form, is the first. Having subdued the perception of inner form is the second. The resolve of the foremost equanimity towards form neither pure nor impure is the third. These three liberations, by attaining mastery over all form, are thereby able to draw out the noble superknowledges — for these superknowledges are not shared with any ordinary being. The resolve of infinite space, the resolve of infinite consciousness, the resolve of nothingness, the resolve of neither perception nor non-perception, and the resolve of a subtle, spontaneously-functioning mind — these five resolves, well cultivated in this sequence, are able to draw out the supreme abiding of the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling.

blocks.text: Fascicle 15 finishes the teachings by number with eights, nines, and tens, and then turns to the other four of the five sciences. Today: the eights. Two lists are especially practical: eight moments when a lazy mind finds excuses (and a diligent mind finds reasons), and the eight worldly winds.

subs.head: The eightfold path as three trainings

blocks.text: "Right speech, right action, and right livelihood are the training of precepts; right mindfulness and right concentration, the training of concentration; right view, thought, and effort, the training of wisdom." Venerable Miào Jìng: mindfulness belongs to both concentration and wisdom, but here it is classed with concentration.

Eight noble persons: those on the four paths and in the four fruits. Venerable Miào Jìng: even the path to stream-entry is already noble; the preparatory stages (heat, summit, patience, supreme mundane) are not counted.

Seven flawed ways to give and one flawless. Flawed giving includes giving "not as one wishes" (Venerable Miào Jìng: giving to secure one's own future wealth). Flawless giving even includes "giving in order to obtain great wealth": Master Cháng Bǎi explains that the bodhisattva seeks wealth "not for his own enjoyment but for beings' needs".

Laziness finds eight excuses in four circumstances: going on almsround, undertaking a task, travelling, and illness. Before and after each: "I'm about to go, so I'll rest"; "I've just come back, so I'll rest." The diligent person finds a reason to practise in the same eight moments. Venerable Miào Jìng: working well when conditions are good is nothing remarkable; only one who meets the causes of laziness and still works is truly diligent.

For those not yet seeking to leave the desire realm, eight desirable rebirths are possible, "comprised within a correct aspiration". Master Cháng Bǎi: the aspiration must match its cause; wanting a human or heavenly rebirth while killing and stealing is not a correct aspiration. Venerable Miào Jìng, candidly, describes "modest" practice: "others keep five precepts, I keep three."

The eight worldly winds again (Day 13). Master Cháng Bǎi: acclaim and blame are to one's face; censure and praise, behind one's back. How does the mind stay unmoved? Venerable Miào Jìng: "If we cultivate the noble path and see all of it as false and empty, praise false, insult false, the mind stays still."

The eight liberations (Day 88) are revisited as eight resolves that draw forth superknowledge and the cessation attainment. Master Cháng Bǎi: non-Buddhists can develop superknowledge, but theirs is unstable; the noble superknowledges are not shared with ordinary beings.

quiz.q: How does the treatise assign the eight limbs of the noble path to the three trainings?
options: right speech, action, livelihood are precepts; right mindfulness and concentration are concentration; right view, intention, diligence are wisdom
right view and intention are precepts; the rest concentration
diligence is precepts; livelihood is wisdom
quiz.why: "Right speech, right action, and right livelihood are called the training of precepts; right mindfulness and right concentration are called the training of concentration; right view, right intention, and right diligence are called the training of wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi: precepts ground concentration, which grounds wisdom.

quiz.q: The eight pure persons are those on the four paths and in the four fruits. Are the stages of heat, summit, patience, and highest worldly dharma included, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: no — even the path to stream-entry is noble; those four stages are excluded, giving eight noble persons
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "The path towards stream-entry is also noble; heat, summit, patience, and the highest worldly dharma are not counted — eight noble persons in all." Master Cháng Bǎi: the correct method is the thirty-seven factors.

quiz.q: Flawless giving includes "giving in order to obtain great wealth." Why is that still flawless, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the bodhisattva seeks wealth not for his own use but for beings' needs, hoping it will kindle their faith in the Dharma
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the bodhisattva gives to obtain great wealth not for his own enjoyment but for beings' needs, hoping it brings them faith in the Dharma. Venerable Miào Jìng: the two motives are compassion and dedication to nirvāṇa; wealth comes naturally.

quiz.q: Laziness arises in eight moments depending on four circumstances. What are they, and what is the fourth?
options: almsround, tasks, travel, and elemental imbalance — the four elements out of balance, i.e., illness
quiz.why: "Namely, depending on almsround, on undertaking a task, on travel, and on bodily imbalance." Master Cháng Bǎi: the fourth is the four elements out of balance — illness, which also triggers laziness. Two moments each make eight.

quiz.q: Per Venerable Miào Jìng, what marks a genuinely diligent person?
options: one who, amid the occasions for laziness, is not lazy and still works
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: working well under normal conditions is nothing remarkable; only one who meets the causes of laziness and still isn't lazy truly works. The treatise: the lazy seem diligent only until an occasion arises.

quiz.q: Among the eight worldly winds, how do censure-and-praise differ from acclaim-and-blame?
options: acclaim and blame are said to one's face; censure and praise behind one's back
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Acclaim and blame are being called good or bad to one's face; censure and praise are being called good or bad behind one's back." Both belong to the situation of effortful action.

quiz.q: How, per Venerable Miào Jìng, does the mind remain unmoved by the eight winds?
options: cultivating the noble path, seeing all as false and empty — praise and insult alike — and the mind stays still
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: if we cultivate the noble path and see all of it as false and empty — praise false, insult false — the mind does not move. Ordinary beings live between joy and sorrow; only the path changes that.
